title: I built a site where nobody can edit their trading track record. Tell me why it won't work.
author: Purple-Ad6867
selftext:
I got tired of signal sellers with screenshot track records. Winners posted, losers deleted.

So I built the opposite. You post a prediction before the open. It gets hash-locked — no backdating. The market settles it automatically. Everything stays: wins, losses, even the entries that never filled. No accounts. Free. Open source.

Almost called it StockOverflow. Went with QuantRank500 — felt more like a race than homework. Everyone gets the same simulated $500. My own bot is user #1.

Two questions for this crowd: what would it take for you to actually trust a record like this? And what's the first way someone will try to game it?

[demo.quantrank500.com](http://demo.quantrank500.com) if you want to poke it. Code's on GitHub.

comments.author: lagoonofl
comments.body: Based solely on reading your post and no further: because you've made a competitive environment with no reward for participating. What if the winner each year got 1k towards a real portfolio?

comments.author: Drakula106
comments.body: Without a ton of people using it, it has no value. And nobody wants to join a site with nobody using it. Chicken egg situation. Better to just track where people are already talking about stocks. xAlphaAudit for X. I wish there was something good for reddit.

replies.author: read_more_comments
replies.body: Plus tradingview let's you post predictions and you can't edit them.

replies.author: Purple-Ad6867
replies.body: chicken-and-egg is real, no argument. but this is more notary than social network — it's useful at n=1. one person gets a verifiable record from day one; the crowd makes it more interesting, not functional.

replies.author: Drakula106
replies.body:
One person really isn't that useful. You want hundreds minimum. Then you can find common ground of good accounts starting to talk about the same stocks early. You'll also have way more stocks to choose from that way too because different clusters of accounts that are good at different things will talk about diverse stocks that all have potential. That's what I'm doing with X. With a really low number you'll have too much variance unless you luck out and end up just blind copying some guy on a heater.

The idea is great but getting people to use the site is not gonna happen. Better off utilizing X, stocktwits, reddit, discord groups, whatever. Just find places people talk stocks and start tracking peoples returns.

replies.author: Purple-Ad6867
replies.body:
you're right on both counts — for signal sourcing you need hundreds of accounts, and getting people to change where they post is brutally hard. no argument.

but I'd say we're solving different halves of the same problem. you're solving discovery: find the good accounts wherever they already talk. I'm solving proof: a record nobody can edit once it's made. those stack — the API here is open, so a tracker like yours could pipe calls into the ledger and get tamper-evident history for free.

site went live yesterday. one user so far: my own bot. so yes, I'm at the "need hundreds, have one" stage — every network in history started there. threads like this are how the word gets out, so genuinely: thanks for engaging with it seriously.

replies.author: Drakula106
replies.body:
I'm saying you can solve proof without developing a social network. I track and verify calls already so no need for help there. 

I wish you luck and would use it if you started to get traction. I'm just saying you are WAY better off cleaning and tracking all the raw data out there rather than building a new source.

comments.author: Sofakingwetoddead
comments.body: That's pretty badass. You're gonna need to corral the top guys into using it. You know the crooked ones won't. :D

replies.author: Purple-Ad6867
replies.body: Thanks, feels good if someone liked the idea. Lets spread it.

replies.author: Purple-Ad6867
replies.body:
true, and that rule is good. but on tradingview an idea is a chart and a story — nobody checks how it ended. there's no score. you "win" by getting likes and followers.

here a prediction is exact numbers — buy at this price, stop here, target there — and the market grades it automatically. your rank comes from your results, not your popularity.

tradingview measures who's interesting. this measures who's right.

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body: Why would anyone use this? Just use myfxbook or trade on the blockchain.

replies.author: Purple-Ad6867
replies.body:
fair points. myfxbook verifies trades you already made, on accounts you choose to publish — link only the winner, delist it when it goes cold. here predictions are committed before the open and can't be unpublished, dead accounts included.

blockchain still needs an oracle for market data, plus wallets and gas to post a thought. a hash chain + public exports gets the same tamper-evidence with no friction.

the no-money point is the fairest. this measures forecasting, not trading — standardized $500 so records compare. for people who can't risk capital yet but can demonstrate skill. if only real-money records count for you, that's legit — this isn't that tool.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body:
I don't think you can modify your account like that to trick myfxbook. At least, I haven't seen it.

By blockchain I meant something like Hyperliquid, that's what I use. You can see all the trades on their block explorer.

How many people do you think don't have $ to trade but have skill, really? Little kids who don't have brokerage accounts?

I just don't understand who you're making this for.

replies.author: Purple-Ad6867
replies.body:
honestly I started out wanting stack overflow for stock predictions — reputation earned from verified answers. it turned into a race instead. same idea either way: prove it in public or it doesn't count.

honestly, predictors aren't the main audience — viewers are. the person staring at Robinhood with $500, drowning in signal sellers and screenshot track records. for them this is a place to look: picks provably locked before the open, every record showing its losses, no way to delete a bad month. the predictors — researchers, students, quant teams — are the smaller group. most people should never post anything. they should just finally have somewhere to check who's actually good.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body:
Fine, even assuming there's a market for this.

You cannot guarantee that someone doesn't pay YOU to change their results. So it has to be a public ledger, like a blockchain. Think about it. And then they can just use a blockchain where you can actually trade.

replies.author: Purple-Ad6867
replies.body: This critique is exactly why I post it in the first place. Hopefully by the time the platform gets traction this will not be in my hands anymore. Maybe a board or a committee.
